This is the second Scummer I've remixed. He makes a great random NPC or supporting character for your role-playing games or miniature games. Don't get me wrong, he could be your character and an epic hero at that. Though he was made to be a bit generic featuring: a rifle/carbine, light armor, and a knife. Scummer #2 here also has a bionic eye and a bionic leg, which can be treated as just cosmetic details. Unless of course, you want them to do more in your games.

Just for an extra bit of fun and functionality, I have included a small random name generator for your scummers in the images above. You know the drill, roll D66 on each of the name tables and then use that to come up with a suitable name. Of course, these tables and the names on them are all just for inspiration. Feel free to pick the names you want, to add your own names to the mix, or change the names in any way that you want. This name generator is a tool, not a box.

You play role-playing games or maybe miniature games (the fun ones with the narrative as central), maybe you play both or some hybrid of the two. So you must find yourself occasionally needing some good guys or bad guys to add to the mayhem. Maybe they are unscrupulous gunmen sent by a local crime boss. Maybe they are stalwart citizens ready to defend their town/neighborhood. Maybe they are the latest member of your space faring crew of adventurers, though you just haven't gotten to know them yet. Maybe they are just hired muscle with guns that your gang hired for a bit of extra firepower in the upcoming battle. Maybe they are just random survivors of the Zombie Apocalypse who could be potential friends or foes. The possibilities are endless for a basic miniature with a firearm (call it a rifle, carbine, or lasgun in this case), some light 'flak' armor, and a combat knife. These NPCs might not be the heroes of the day, but they can't be completely ignored either.

Here are twelve, perhaps crude, though definitely brutal close combat hand-to-hand melee assault weapons. They are intended to allow give you some extra options and conversion bits for your Chaos Cultists. You do love Chaos Cultists don't you?? Though I think they are generic enough to work for most human sized miniatures in any grim and dark dystopian future setting from undercity gangs, to wasteland scavengers, rebels, organized criminal thugs, and pretty much any kind of poorly equipped ne'er-do-wells up to no good.

Here are the 12 unique weapons:

-- Axe
-- Club
-- Hammer1
-- Hammer2
-- Knife1
-- Knife2
-- Mace
-- Pick
-- Pipe
-- Scimitar
-- Sword1
-- Sword2

Each weapon comes in three STL variants:
1) weapon by itself
2) weapon held in a right hand
3) weapon held in a right hand (hand has a nub to socket into wrists)

Knife1 and Knife2 have four variants each, two with the blade held normally and two with the blade held ready to stab. You can mirror the weapons with hands on them to create left-handed versions. All total that comes to 68 different options. You can use these files for physical or digital conversions as you see fit. They are also Creative Common Licensed so that you can modify them as you please and then share your own innovations.

Enjoy, and may the Dark Gods favor you.

This revised version of my old Autopistol STL has some subtle changes that I like. I also added a few variants with different hands attached for easy conversions. In a grimdark science fantasy universe such a weapon as this might be found in the hands of chaotic cultists, undercity gang members, Imperial officials, militia troopers, organized criminals, xeno cultists, merchants and their guards, household troops, and many more. For physically converting or digitally remixing miniatures this one pistol has many potential uses.

I made some changes to my existing Autopistol Model 302 STL. I took most of my inspiration for the original design from a couple images I found online. I liked the look overall, though I felt like the end of the barrel was maybe inclined to break off if dropped. So for this version I changed the proportions so that the muzzle break in front of the weapon connected very slightly to the angled front of the forward handgrip on the pistol. Looking at other images online, I also decided to shorten the pistol's ammo magazine. Previously the magazine extended below the pistol grip, but now it stops just short of being equal in length to the pistol grip. The width and height of the pistol remain the same, but I shortened the overall length from 12mm to 11.5mm which I think makes it scaled a bit better for most plastic, resin, and STL miniatures out there.

Here's a link to the original version.

Autopistol - Model 302 -by- Scavvon

Here is another one of the true heroes of a grim and dark science fantasy setting, where no one will be missed. That's right, it's another feisty chaos cultist fighting the good fight. He knows he won't be missed, but then again did anyone even notice him the first place. Grim, like I said. However, contrary to the stories that you've been told, each human life isn't valuable solely for the sacrifice it can ultimately make some far away half-dead God King. With determination, some luck, and the favor of the Dark Gods every human has a small chance of escaping the lot fate has given them. And that includes even lowly and humble citizens of the dying Empire, it even includes mere mortal cultists.

When servants of the Inquistion must hunt heretics in the dangerous depths of the undercity it never hurts to have some extra firepower. That's were the Servile Cyborg with Sizable Gun comes in. This single-minded automaton can pack as much firepower as a crew served heavy weapon team. He never complains, but he rarely takes any initiative either. In fact, he performs best with a bit of guidance from his friends. He can be equipped with a selection of three devastating heavy weapons depending on your needs. The ODV Heavy Blaster launches bursts of high caliber dual-mode projectiles that are equally effective against armored or unarmored targets. One shot from this weapon is more than enough to deal with a measely chaotic cultist. The opposite end of the spectrum is the mighty Multi-Mazer Melta-Beamer. This weapon hits just one target, but it hits extremely hard! Definitely a waste when targeting a wimpy chaotic cultist, but hulking mutant abominations or vile places of worship for the followers are the Dark Gods are ideal targets. The final weapon option is the Phased Plasma Projector, this weapon is the happy medium of overkill. It hits like a cargo-8 and covers an area wide enough to catch multiple targets. As an additional benefit this particular Servile Cyborg's Sizable Guns each have unique enhancements to improve their reliability. Because let's face it, there is never a techno-guru around when you need one, let alone when you are in the heart of darkness battling heretics.

The Mystical Missionary is a steadfast and zealous henchman ready to serve the God Emperor and any worthy inquisitor in his service. Before his recruitment to the inquisition this individual traveled the galaxy visiting any and all human worlds to spread the the God Emperor's light. He has been exposed to many different sects and devotions who all worship the God Emperor. He has witnessed miracles, received divine knowledge from secretive cults, and also his own God Emperor touched visions. The Mystical Missionary is a proven fighter, especially against the forces of Chaos. Though his greatest strengths are his exemplary faith in the God Emperor, his inspirational presence, and his profound knowledge of esoteric mysteries.

This model is dedicated to my followers. I have recently hit and surpassed 100 followers. Thank you for your support.

------------------

A savage and brutal ogre once lived a happy and fulfilled life on his feral homeworld. Though still young he had beaten, bashed, and smashed his way in to the ranks of his tribe's most feared warriors. His weapon of choice was a massive heavy club with vicious spikes protruding from it. These happy days were not to last however. Ships descended from the sky and other ogres along with men rounded up the ogres and took them away.

The 'recruitment officers' determined that this ogre would serve in the Imperial space army. His beloved club was taken from him and he was forced to carry a massive gun instead. The ogre was not happy. He was given opportunities to fight, which he relished, but he had to obey the rules and orders of the men in uniforms. He hated these puny men with their rules and shouted orders.

Not for the first time, he and the other ogres and men in his unit were sent to a new world to fight. This fight was long and victory did not come. Many ogres and men were killed in the following months. Soon the ogre was the only ogre left from his squad. He was assigned to a new squad of puny men, these men were called troublemakers and malcontents. They too had all come together from other squads that no longer existed. Conditions in the trenches had grown very bad by this point; ammunition, food, warm clothes, and other essentials were in short supply. The enemy was bombarding their positions with artillery every day all the while freezing rain poured from the sky.

The puny men in his squad were not like others of their kind. They were clever and did things against orders to stay alive. They treated the ogre as one of their own, they respected his strength and might. So, one night when his new squad decided at last to leave their posts and not return the ogre joined them. The squad made their way to a devastated city. The two armies were not fighting in the city. However, the residence of the city as well as groups of deserters from both armies were there. These three groups, in small bands fought one another for survival. They fought for food, weapons, ammo, supplies, and dominance. The ogre and his friends, they no longer used the term squad, fought constantly. They defeated other groups of locals, and deserters from both sides.

His friends found new gods who rewarded those who worshipped them, especially those who were victorious in their names. Shortly thereafter, in the spoils from a defeated foe, a massive power maul was taken. The ogre claimed it for himself, no one else could wield it anyway. The power maul was big, heavy, and crackled with destructive energy. It also had vicious spikes protruding from it. With this weapon the ogre killed many foes in the name of the new gods. The ogre was now among the elite warriors of his new group. Later a massive symbol of the new gods was found. It was in the shape of an eight pointed star with a ring connecting them and it was made from wrought iron. His friends told the ogre that it was a magical relic from their new gods. A ritual was performed and the iron star was merged with the ogre's body. Now he could feel their power and strength surging through him. He also rapidly healed any wounds he suffered. After that with the power maul and the iron star in his body the ogre was even more lethal. He and the his friends fought and won many battles. The new gods saw the ogre's many victories and the foes he had slain. They rewarded him with a magical blessing so that one of his hands became a giant claw. The claw was strong and useful in battle. At last, the ogre was happy once again, happier than he had ever been.

Note: I have also included STL files for the Power Maul, both a pristine and a damaged version.

The chaos cultist who would go on to become known as Daemonlash was a solitary and taciturn individual. Despite his reserved manner this cultist was a skilled warrior and a gifted leader. One day he challenged the leader of his chaos cult to a fight to see who would lead the cult. He was handily defeated by the current cult leader. A certain amount of shame came with being thus defeated, but a more serious problem came with this development. The existing cult leader now saw this cultist as a potential threat, maybe he would make a challenge again one day and win. Everyone in the cult knew that their cult leader would almost certainly maneuver things so that his most recent challenger was never a threat again. Knowing this, the defeated challenger volunteered to become a living host for a warp daemon. As a barely sane living weapon for the Dark Powers the former cultist was no longer a threat to the cult leader's position, but at least he was alive.

The daemon that possessed the cultist who would become known as Daemonlash had a peculiar way of not making any outward changes to his host's physical body. Only when in combat would the daemon transmute his host's flesh in the form of grotesque fleshy tentacles that suddenly burst from the cultist's chest. These tentacles shot forward with explosive speed to entangle, rend, and strangle his foes. At these times the cultist's head would also transform to a ghastly cackling daemonic visage. And thus was born the daemon-infused mutant cultist know as 'Daemonlash.'

I have never really liked space marines, it's much more fun to play the underdogs. Also, when it comes to choosing a faction, I find it more fun to play the bad guys. Translate this into a certain grim future setting and you come up with the ultimate bad guy underdogs... Chaos Cultists.

This is the first of what I plan to be a long series of more Chaos Cultists. I mean c'mon, if you tell someone your genetically modified gene enhanced super soldiers in power armor with the best weapons and training possible won a battle, who cares? That is what they are supposed to do. But you tell someone that your hordes of Chaos Cultists defeated, well, anything, then that is a truly impressive victory.

Aside from the obvious cool factor, why might you want to collect Chaos Cultists? Well, as miniatures go they are tremendously useful and versatile. Obviously they have a place on the brutal battlefields of the grim future (where there is only war). What about the close quarters skirmishes pitting one murderous team against another? Chaos Cultists certainly belong in the shadowed depths of the undercity. And for that matter, they belong on every planet in the confines of the empire and beyond, they are the archenemy after all. Suppose you are playing a modern day miniature adventure where a group of fearless individuals battle cosmic horrors from beyond space and time? You are definitely going to need some cultists for that. I could go on, but I think you get the picture. Chaos Cultists might not be the most effective troops, but they are certainly the coolest.

The cultist who would go on to be known as 'Talon' was scrawny and puny. He was constantly being bullied by the local thugs and gangers in his poor neighborhood. He joined a chaotic cult in hopes of a better life and to escape the foul treatment of his tormentors. Alas, he found that he had only traded one set of bullying torturers for another, for in the chaotic cult strength and power were prized and weakness reviled. The cultist sought out the legendary Master of Possession, Faustus Daemoncaller who was at that time visiting his world in secret. Daemoncaller was only too happy to perform the dreadful and perverse ritual upon the young seeker.

Once joined with the daemon it learned of his past experience and history. Perhaps it was compassion that made the daemon within him transform his body into a massive and brutishly muscled thing with one oversized arm ending in a savage claw. Or perhaps the daemon sensing the dark emotions of it's host, his rage, hatred, and sense of weakness that the daemon fed upon and transformed the young cultist into a form ideal for enacting bloody revenge on all those who had previously plagued him.

After that the cultist earned the name Talon based on his new form and his keen desire to maliciously destroy any who gained his ire. Not long after the old neighbor where Talon was raised became the site of a series of brutal and savage murders which continued for weeks only to end as suddenly as they had began. The unknown perpetrators, or perpetrator, was never identified or apprehended.

Would any of them really be worth calling cultists if they didn't have their Big Stubbers? I've decided to build an army of Frateris Militia led by an Apostate Cardinal. Let's be honest, Frateris Militia are basically imperial cultists. And as such, they will need their own Big Stubbers, lots of Big Stubbers.

I started with LoggyK's excellent Heavy Gun for this design and I just kept adding details until I had the look of a xeno-cultist Big Stubber. The final model is sort of a mix of old and new. The scale should be 1-1.
